In [[functional analysis]], the '''Borel graph theorem''' is generalization of the [[closed graph theorem]] that was proven by L. Schwartz.{{sfn|Trèves|2006|p=549}}

The Borel graph theorem shows that the [[Closed graph theorem (functional analysis)|closed graph theorem]] is valid for [[linear map]]s defined on and valued in most spaces encountered in analysis.{{sfn|Trèves|2006|p=549}} 

==Statement==

A [[topological space]] is called a [[Polish space]] if it is a [[Separable space|separable]] [[complete metrizable space]] and that a [[Souslin space]] is the continuous image of a Polish space. The weak [[Continuous dual space|dual]] of a [[Separable space|separable]] [[Fréchet space]] and the [[Strong dual space|strong dual]] of a separable [[Fréchet–Montel space]] are Souslin spaces. Also, the space of distributions and all [[Lp-space]]s over open subsets of [[Euclidean space]] as well as many other spaces that occur in analysis are Souslin spaces. The Borel graph theorem states:{{sfn|Trèves|2006|p=549}}

:Let <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> be [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] [[Locally convex topological vector space|locally convex]] spaces and let <math>u : X \to Y</math> be linear. If <math>X</math> is the [[inductive limit]] of an arbitrary family of [[Banach space]]s, if <math>Y</math> is a Souslin space, and if the graph of <math>u</math> is a Borel set in <math>X \times Y,</math> then <math>u</math> is continuous.

==Generalization==

An improvement upon this theorem, proved by A. Martineau, uses K-analytic spaces. A topological space <math>X</math> is called a <math>K_{\sigma \delta}</math> if it is the countable intersection of countable unions of [[Compact space|compact set]]s. A Hausdorff topological space <math>Y</math> is called '''{{visible anchor|K-analytic}}''' if it is the continuous image of a <math>K_{\sigma \delta}</math> space (that is, if there is a <math>K_{\sigma \delta}</math> space <math>X</math> and a [[continuous map]] of <math>X</math> onto <math>Y</math>). Every compact set is K-analytic so that there are non-separable K-analytic spaces.
Also, every Polish, Souslin, and [[Reflexive space|reflexive]] [[Fréchet space]] is K-analytic as is the weak dual of a Fréchet space. The generalized theorem states:{{sfn|Trèves|2006|pp=557–558}}

:Let <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> be locally convex Hausdorff spaces and let <math>u : X \to Y</math> be linear. If <math>X</math> is the inductive limit of an arbitrary family of Banach spaces, if <math>Y</math> is a K-analytic space, and if the graph of <math>u</math> is closed in <math>X \times Y,</math> then <math>u</math> is continuous.
